name: Landing Page Layout (Marketing)
description: A marketing landing page from the header to the footer: a header that sticks with CSS alone and can turn solid as the page scrolls, calls to action that are links named by their visible text, social proof from the user's real content, and motion that never leaves a section hidden.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

layout.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The header is a sticky bar; the menu is a modal.

positioningContract.header: Sticky at the top, in the page's flow; scroll-padding-top at its height
positioningContract.hero: The first section; pulled up under the header by its height when the header starts transparent
positioningContract.sections: In source order, in the page's normal flow
positioningContract.footer: At the end of the page, scrolling with it

invariants: The page scrolls, not a box inside it
scroll-padding-top at the header's height keeps focused elements and link targets clear of the sticky header
Nothing scrolls sideways down to 320 px wide, and no section hides its overflow
Every section is visible without script, under reduced motion, and when printing

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend a marketing landing page: a sticky header, a hero, features, social proof, an optional pricing section, a closing call to action, and a footer. Calls to action are links named by their visible text; testimonials, logos, and numbers are the user's real content; motion is optional and never leaves a section hidden. Build on the project's header, section, card, and button components when it has suitable ones. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: A header that sticks with CSS alone, with scroll-padding-top at its height and a skip link; optionally transparent over the hero until the page scrolls
Below 1024 px, the links in a native dialog, as in the Navigation Bar guide
Calls to action that are links, named by their visible text (WCAG 2.5.3)
Social proof from the user's real content, or marked placeholders; nothing invented
A hero that is visible at load, with a high-priority image and sizes on every image
An optional scroll reveal that hides nothing without script, under reduced motion, or when printing
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, the router, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has a header, sections, cards, or buttons, configure or extend them to meet this guide instead of building others, and keep their APIs.
2. Collect the content: the user's copy, testimonials, logos, and numbers. Where any are missing, use marked placeholders and ask for the real ones (implementationDetails.content).
3. Lay out the sections in order with their headings (structure, layoutModel).
4. Build the header (components.Header, frameworkPatterns.stickyHeader) and its menu below 1024 px (components.Header.behavior.menu).
5. Build the hero, the features, and the social proof (components.Hero, components.Features, components.SocialProof), with the calls to action as links (implementationDetails.callsToAction).
6. Add the optional parts the task asks for: the email signup (implementationDetails.signup), the scroll reveal (frameworkPatterns.scrollReveal).
7. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, 200% zoom, and reduced motion, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

Header.description: Sticky: the skip link, the logo, the main navigation, and one call to action; the Menu button below 1024 px

Hero.description: The h1, the subheadline, the calls to action, and the product image or video

Features.description: An h2 and a grid of feature cards

SocialProof.description: Testimonials, client logos, or numbers, from the user

ClosingCta.description: A short heading, a sentence, and the primary call to action

Footer.description: Link groups, social links, and the legal line

StatusRegion.description: One polite status region, present from the start, for the email signup's result

Header.description: The header starts with a skip link, "Skip to content", shown while it has focus and going to <main id="main" tabindex="-1"> (WCAG 2.4.1). Then the logo, a link to the home page named with the site's name, a <nav> labelled "Main", and one call to action.

behavior.sticky: position: sticky; top: 0 keeps the header at the top without a script and keeps its space in the page. A fixed header takes no space, so the page would need padding that matches its height. scroll-padding-top on the root element, set to the header's height, scrolls focused elements and in-page link targets clear of it (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11).
behavior.transparentOverHero: Optional: the header starts transparent over the hero and turns solid once the page has scrolled past a threshold. The hero is pulled up under the header by the header's height. An IntersectionObserver on a sentinel at the top of the page, as tall as the threshold, switches it, with no scroll listener. At exactly the threshold, the sentinel's edge still touches the window, so the header turns solid one pixel later (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Without script, the header stays solid.
behavior.contrast: The header's text meets 4.5:1 in both states: in the transparent state against the hero behind it, the lightest part of a hero image included.
behavior.menu: Below 1024 px, the links move into a menu opened by a Menu button, and from 1024 px the header shows them: one switch, as in the Navigation Bar guide. The menu is a native <dialog> opened with showModal() and named "Main menu", so the rest of the page is inert, Escape closes it, and focus returns to Menu. It has a visible Close button ("Close menu"), and closes when a link in it is followed. A click on the backdrop closes it as in the Modal Dialog guide: the <dialog> has no padding of its own (an inner wrapper has it), so only the backdrop makes the dialog the click's target, and the press has to start on the backdrop too. A rule that checks only the target also closes the menu on a click on its padding, and on a drag from inside it onto the backdrop (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Menu and Close are at least 44 px square on touch screens.

Hero.description: The headline, a short subheadline, the calls to action, and a product image or video. On phones they stack in that order; from 1024 px, text and media sit side by side.

dimensions.headlinePx: 48 to 64 from 1024 px, 32 to 40 on phones

behavior.visibleAtLoad: The headline and the image are visible at load. They're usually the Largest Contentful Paint, so they don't fade in from opacity 0.
behavior.images: The hero image is never lazy-loaded and gets fetchpriority="high". Every image gets width and height, so nothing shifts while images load, and srcset with sizes when it comes in several widths.
behavior.textOverImage: Text over an image gets an overlay or a scrim that keeps it at 4.5:1, checked over the lightest part of the image.
behavior.video: A background video is muted and playsinline, has a visible pause button (WCAG 2.2.2), and doesn't play on its own under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, where its poster image shows. A demo video with speech has captions.

Features.description: A grid from CSS alone, such as repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(16rem, 100%), 1fr)), or one, two, and three columns at 768 and 1024 px. It needs no resize handler.

behavior.cards: Each card has a decorative icon (aria-hidden="true"), an <h3>, and a short description.
behavior.many: More than six features: a second row, not a carousel or tabs. A carousel hides features behind controls, and one that turns on its own needs a pause button (WCAG 2.2.2).

SocialProof.description: Testimonials, client logos, or numbers, all from the user.

behavior.testimonials: A testimonial is a <figure> with the quote in a <blockquote> and the name, role, and company in a <figcaption>. The name isn't a heading. An avatar beside the name is decorative (alt=""), or the name is read twice.
behavior.logos: Client logos are a list of images, each named after its company ("Acme"), not "logo".
behavior.numbers: Numbers (customers, uptime, ratings) come from the user, with their source; they're claims like any other.
behavior.none: With no testimonials yet, leave the section out, or show a logo list; never fill it with invented quotes.

ClosingCta.description: A short heading, one sentence, and the page's primary call to action, again as a link.

Footer.description: Link groups under headings, social links named after their service ("Acme on GitHub", saying so when they open a new tab), and the legal line. It scrolls with the page.

desktop.hero: Text and media side by side
desktop.grids: Three columns, or as many as fit

tablet.header: The Menu button and the menu dialog
tablet.hero: Stacked, media below the calls to action

mobile.header: The Menu button and the menu dialog
mobile.hero: Stacked: headline, subheadline, calls to action, media
mobile.grids: One column; nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px wide

resizeHandling.approach: CSS does the layout at every width. The menu reacts to a change of matchMedia('(min-width: 1024px)'), not to resize events: widening closes it, as the Navigation Bar guide says.

headerSolid.description: Whether the header is solid. Only with the optional transparent state.
headerSolid.determination: An IntersectionObserver on the sentinel at the top of the page: transparent while it is in view

menuOpen.description: Whether the menu dialog is open, below 1024 px.

signupStatus.description: The email signup's state, when the page has one.

ssrConsiderations.header: Render the header solid; the script makes it transparent at the top of the page.
ssrConsiderations.reveal: Render every section visible; the script hides only sections still below the window once the page has loaded.

navigationBehavior.inPageLinks: Links to sections (#features) land below the header through scroll-padding-top. Smooth scrolling only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

mobileSafeArea.notes: On phones with a notch, env(safe-area-inset-top) pads the header only when the viewport meta tag has viewport-fit=cover; without it, the values are 0.

motionPreferences.prefersReducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing is hidden or slides, the header changes without a fade, in-page links jump, and a background video shows its poster.

overflowPolicy.page: No sideways scrolling, down to 320 px wide
overflowPolicy.sections: Don't hide overflow on sections. overflow-x: hidden makes the other axis compute to auto, so the section becomes a scroll container, and a sticky element inside it sticks to the section instead of the page (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Fix what overflows; if something has to be cut, overflow-x: clip doesn't make a scroll container.

scrollReveal.note: It observes with threshold 0 and no root margin. A threshold is a share of the section, so with 0.1 a section taller than ten windows never shows, and a root shrunk at the bottom never meets a short last section at the end of the page (both checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Focus in a section shows it at once: a waiting section skips the fade, which would start it at opacity 0, and a fade that's under way ends, through transition: none on the section while it has focus. That rule covers every section, not only fading ones, so a transition the project gives the section doesn't fade it in either, and it has to win over that transition. It has to be none: only a property that leaves transition-property cancels its running transition, and a zero duration leaves the fade running (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit).

hover.note: A hover lift on cards and buttons is optional; under reduced motion, use a color change instead.

animations.reducedMotion: Nothing is hidden and nothing slides under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

requirements.1.1.1: Images have alt text that says what they show; decorative images, and avatars beside a name, have alt="".
requirements.1.2.2: A video with speech has captions.
requirements.1.3.1: Landmarks, one h1, and an h2 per section; testimonials are figures with a blockquote.
requirements.1.4.3: Text meets 4.5:1, text over images included.
requirements.1.4.10: At 320 px wide nothing scrolls sideways.
requirements.1.4.11: Focus indicators and the outlines of secondary calls to action meet 3:1.
requirements.2.2.2: A background video, or anything that moves on its own, has a pause button.
requirements.2.4.1: A skip link goes past the header to the main area.
requirements.2.4.4: Calls to action say where they go.
requirements.2.4.11: scroll-padding-top keeps a focused element clear of the sticky header.
requirements.2.5.3: A call to action's accessible name starts with its visible text.
requirements.4.1.3: The email signup's result goes to one polite status region.

keyboardNavigation.order: The skip link, the header, then each section in order, then the footer: the order on screen.
keyboardNavigation.menu: Escape closes the menu, and focus returns to Menu.

screenReader.callsToAction: Its visible text says where it goes ("Start free trial", "Book a demo"), and nothing replaces that text as its name: an aria-label that differs from the visible text fails WCAG 2.5.3, since voice control users say what they see. Where two calls to action read the same but go to different places, add visually hidden words after the visible text ("Get started", then hidden "with Professional").
screenReader.testimonials: A testimonial is a <figure> with the quote in a <blockquote> and the name, role, and company in a <figcaption>. The name isn't a heading. An avatar beside the name is decorative (alt=""), or the name is read twice.

focusManagement.notObscured: position: sticky; top: 0 keeps the header at the top without a script and keeps its space in the page. A fixed header takes no space, so the page would need padding that matches its height. scroll-padding-top on the root element, set to the header's height, scrolls focused elements and in-page link targets clear of it (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11).
focusManagement.menu: The menu is a native <dialog> opened with showModal() and named "Main menu", so the rest of the page is inert, Escape closes it, and focus returns to Menu. It has a visible Close button ("Close menu"), and closes when a link in it is followed.

colorContrast.note: See designSystem.colors; check the project's own colors, and text over images, the same way.

designSystem.note: Suggested defaults for projects without a design. The project's tokens and existing components win; check its colors meet the same contrast.

light.text: #111827 for headings (17.7:1 on white), #374151 for body text (10.3:1), #4b5563 for muted text (7.6:1, and 7.2:1 on #f9fafb)
light.primaryCta: #2563eb with #ffffff text (5.2:1); #3b82f6 is only 3.7:1. A green call to action needs #047857 (5.5:1); #10b981 is only 2.5:1.

typography.headline: 48 to 64 px from 1024 px, 32 to 40 px on phones, weight 700 to 800, line height 1.1 to 1.2

implementationDetails.content: The page uses the user's real copy, testimonials, client logos, and numbers. Where the task doesn't give them, use placeholders that look like placeholders, such as "[Customer quote]" and "[Name, role, company]", and ask for the real ones. Never invent testimonials, customer names, logos, ratings, or statistics. Invented social proof misleads visitors, and fake reviews and testimonials are against consumer protection rules in the US and the EU.
implementationDetails.callsToAction: A call to action that goes to a page (sign up, book a demo, see pricing) is a link (<a href>). A button is only for an action on this page, such as opening a dialog. Its visible text says where it goes ("Start free trial", "Book a demo"), and nothing replaces that text as its name: an aria-label that differs from the visible text fails WCAG 2.5.3, since voice control users say what they see. Where two calls to action read the same but go to different places, add visually hidden words after the visible text ("Get started", then hidden "with Professional"). One primary call to action per section; the secondary one is outlined or a text link.
implementationDetails.socialProof: A testimonial is a <figure> with the quote in a <blockquote> and the name, role, and company in a <figcaption>. The name isn't a heading. An avatar beside the name is decorative (alt=""), or the name is read twice. Client logos are a list of images, each named after its company ("Acme"), not "logo". Numbers (customers, uptime, ratings) come from the user, with their source; they're claims like any other. With no testimonials yet, leave the section out, or show a logo list; never fill it with invented quotes.
implementationDetails.signup: Optional, in the hero or the closing section. The field has a visible label, not just a placeholder, type="email", and autocomplete="email"; the text says what people sign up for and how often they'll hear from you. Its result ("Check your inbox to confirm") and its errors go to one polite status region that's in the page from the start; a field error goes in the field's description, as the Form Validation Pattern says.
implementationDetails.motion: All motion is optional. The scroll reveal fades sections in as they reach the window. It hides only what it can show again: sections still below the window once the page has loaded and the browser has restored its scroll position, on screens, when motion is allowed. After a reload or Back, WebKit restores the position only after the load event, so a section hidden earlier blinks out and fades back in (checked). Without script, under reduced motion, and when printing, nothing is hidden. It observes with threshold 0 and no root margin. A threshold is a share of the section, so with 0.1 a section taller than ten windows never shows, and a root shrunk at the bottom never meets a short last section at the end of the page (both checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Focus in a section shows it at once: a waiting section skips the fade, which would start it at opacity 0, and a fade that's under way ends, through transition: none on the section while it has focus. That rule covers every section, not only fading ones, so a transition the project gives the section doesn't fade it in either, and it has to win over that transition. It has to be none: only a property that leaves transition-property cancels its running transition, and a zero duration leaves the fade running (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). The hero never fades in, since it holds the largest paint. Smooth scrolling for in-page links goes in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference). Turn each animation off where it's defined, rather than with one rule for every element: a reset that removes all animations leaves keyframe-based reveals stuck on their first frame. A hover lift on cards and buttons is optional; under reduced motion, use a color change instead.
implementationDetails.overflow: At 320 px wide nothing scrolls sideways, and long headlines wrap (overflow-wrap: break-word). Don't hide overflow on sections. overflow-x: hidden makes the other axis compute to auto, so the section becomes a scroll container, and a sticky element inside it sticks to the section instead of the page (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Fix what overflows; if something has to be cut, overflow-x: clip doesn't make a scroll container.
implementationDetails.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The header is a sticky bar; the menu is a modal.
implementationDetails.appearance: Suggested defaults; the project's design and tokens win. Content up to 1200 px wide, centered; section padding 96 px from 1024 px and 48 px on phones; grid gaps 32 px and 24 px. The headline 48 to 64 px from 1024 px and 32 to 40 px on phones, line height 1.1 to 1.2; section headings 32 to 40 px; body text 16 to 18 px at line height 1.5. Calls to action at least 24 px tall, 44 px suggested, with a 2 px focus outline at a 2 px offset.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version. The header's links, dropdowns, and menu are in the Navigation Bar guide.

stickyHeader.description: The sticky header with scroll-padding-top at its height, transparent over the hero until the page has scrolled 48 px: an IntersectionObserver on a sentinel switches it, and without script it stays solid.
stickyHeader.html:
Skip to content Acme

Reports your whole team reads

scrollReveal.description: An optional scroll reveal that hides only sections still below the window once the page has loaded and its scroll position is restored, on screens and when motion is allowed; threshold 0 and no root margin, so tall and short sections show; and focus shows a section at once, without the fade or in the middle of one (transition: none while it has focus).

edgeCases.noProof: Leave the section out, or show a list of client logos; never invent them.
edgeCases.manyFeatures: A second row of cards, not a carousel.
edgeCases.longHeadline: It wraps on phones; shorten it before making the text smaller than 32 px.
edgeCases.noScript: Every section is visible and the header is solid. Below 1024 px the menu needs the script, so keep the main pages reachable without it too, such as from the footer.
edgeCases.pricingSection: The Pricing Table guide covers the billing choice and the plans.

must: Build on the project's header, section, card, and button components when they're suitable, and keep their APIs
Use the user's real testimonials, logos, and numbers, or placeholders marked as such
Make calls to action that go to a page links, named by their visible text
Let the header stick with CSS, with scroll-padding-top at its height
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Invent testimonials, customer names, logos, ratings, or statistics
Add a dependency, such as an animation or scroll library, without asking
Hide a section before the script runs, under reduced motion, or when printing
Fade in the hero, or lazy-load its image
Give a call to action an aria-label that replaces its visible text
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: The page starts with a skip link to the main area, and has one h1, the hero's headline, with an h2 for each section
The header sticks with CSS alone, and a link focused under it, or a section reached by an in-page link, is scrolled clear of it (scroll-padding-top at its height)
A header that starts transparent over the hero turns solid once the page has scrolled past the threshold, stays solid without script, and its text meets 4.5:1 in both states
Below 1024 px, a Menu button opens the links in a native dialog named "Main menu"; Close, Escape, a click that starts and ends on the backdrop, and a followed link close it, and focus returns to Menu
Calls to action that go to a page are links, and each one's accessible name starts with its visible text
Testimonials, logos, and numbers are the user's real content, or placeholders marked as such; nothing is invented
Testimonials are figures with a blockquote and a figcaption; an avatar beside its name has empty alt text, and logos are named after their company
The hero's headline and image are visible at load; the hero image has fetchpriority="high", and every image has width and height
A background video has a visible pause button and doesn't play on its own under reduced motion; a video with speech has captions

Without script, under reduced motion, and when printing, every section is visible; with the scroll reveal, nothing in view is ever hidden, after a reload or Back included, a section fades in once any part of it scrolls into view, and focus shows it at once, mid-fade included
The grids come from CSS alone, nothing scrolls sideways at 320 px wide, and no section hides its overflow
An email signup has a visible label, type="email" with autocomplete="email", and gives its result in the status region
Text meets 4.5:1 and focus indicators 3:1 against every section's background, text over images included
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens
